findings.headline: The title reads like a form label, not an invitation
findings.evidence: Member's Mark Boxer Briefs Feedback Survey
findings.explanation: The title identifies the product, but uses title case and a generic feedback-survey label. Use sentence case, keeping Member's Mark capitalized, and invite members to share their experience.
findings.member_impact: A clear, inviting title helps members understand the topic and feel welcome before they begin.

findings.headline: The welcome does not explain what you want to learn or why members were invited
findings.evidence: Welcome to the Boxer Briefs Survey!
findings.explanation: The welcome names the product but does not describe the focus or explain the invitation. Add what you want to learn and the actual reason these members were selected. Confirm the selection basis before publishing; do not imply a verified purchase unless that is known.
findings.member_impact: Members cannot tell why their experience is relevant or what kind of feedback you need.

findings.headline: Members are asked to complete a survey, not help shape the product
findings.evidence: Welcome to the Boxer Briefs Survey!
findings.explanation: Add a clear invitation to help improve the product. Frame members as partners whose everyday experience can guide improvements, without promising that every suggestion will be adopted. This can be combined with the introduction rewrite.
findings.member_impact: Members may feel like respondents filling out a form rather than partners contributing useful ideas.

findings.headline: The final message sounds like a system status
findings.explanation: Replace the impersonal status message with a direct, human acknowledgment. Keep this conversational improvement alongside the separate additions for gratitude and how feedback will be used.
findings.member_impact: After sharing personal opinions, members reach an abrupt ending that feels automated rather than conversational.

findings.headline: The ending never thanks members for their time
findings.explanation: Add an explicit thank-you that recognizes the time and product experience members contributed, rather than only confirming completion.
findings.member_impact: Members receive no acknowledgment of the effort they put into answering, including the written responses.

findings.headline: Members are not told what happens with their answers
findings.explanation: Add a concrete, accurate account of how feedback will inform product decisions. Confirm the intended use with the research team before publishing. Do not promise changes or a follow-up unless those are planned. Combine this sentence with the thank-you and warmer closing.
findings.member_impact: Members leave without knowing whether their answers will be useful or how their participation can make a difference.
